focus: What I learn about AI as a student who builds with it

inbox.summary: Got my OS midterm back (84), and my roommate's databases slides broke the study helper.
Fixed the language bug with one line, then reran all 41 test questions.
A first-year asked me how to start learning AI, and my answer was messy.
Tried a cheaper model for quiz mode. Fine questions, way too generous grading.
Took my OS midterm. Having the study helper quiz me beat asking it questions.
Added lecture titles to every chunk, and stopped it making up exam answers.
Shared the study helper with 12 classmates. They asked things I never tested.
A new model got 17 of my 20 questions to my setup's 16, at 3x the cost. Not switching.
First AI club meeting. I couldn't explain what makes something an agent.
Started asking ChatGPT for hints instead of solutions.
Took my first algorithms quiz without ChatGPT. It went badly.
My OS professor is fine with AI for studying, as long as we can explain our answers.
The study helper was wrong half the time, so I wrote 20 test questions.
Section-sized chunks and slides-only answers made the study helper much better.
Rewrote my parser myself. Messier, but I can explain every line.
At office hours I couldn't explain the parser the AI wrote for me.
Got the first version of my study helper answering from my OS slides.
Searched my OS notes with embeddings, and they finally clicked.
Read about embeddings for the third time. Still didn't get it.
